items.name: ripple
items.title: Ripple
items.description: Vue directive for a Material-style press ripple that grows from the press point and drifts to the centre.
items.docs:
This is a Vue directive, so it does nothing until you register it. Add it once in your app entry:

  import vRipple from '@/lib/ripple'
  app.directive('ripple', vRipple)

Then use it anywhere: <Button v-ripple>Press me</Button>. Pass false to disable it, or an object to tint it: v-ripple="{ color: 'red', opacity: 0.3 }".

The host element must establish a containing block; the directive sets position: relative on it only if it is still static.

items.docs:
The root is contain: size, so it takes no height from its content by default. Give it an explicit height (h-72, or any other value) or it collapses to nothing.

Put padding on a wrapper inside the slot, not on the root's class. The bars are positioned against the root while the geometry that drives them is measured from the scrolling viewport inside it, so padding on the root shifts the bars out of alignment with the content they represent. A border on the root is fine — only padding shifts them.

Set virtualize and pass items to render long lists. The default slot then receives { item, index } and is rendered once per row in the rendered window, which is the visible rows plus a small overscan buffer. Without virtualize the slot renders once and its scope carries no item.

The area scrolls on one axis, set by orientation (vertical by default): it sets the viewport's overflow, the virtualized axis and which scrollbar renders, so content that must scroll sideways needs orientation="horizontal". virtualize also accepts an options object: estimateSize, overscan, lanes, gap, scrollMargin and getScrollElement.
